text:
emily: Heads-up - onboarding sample using Kotlin Flow + Retrofit shows duplicate token refresh attempts when the network blips during collection. Backend sees two /refresh-token hits for one expired-token event.

emily: Repro: viewModel launches a Flow that maps to `service.getData()` suspended calls and `collectLatest`. If connection drops briefly, we sometimes issue two refreshes.

raj: Interesting. Is the Flow using `retryWhen` or `catch` that might re-trigger the upstream? collectLatest cancels previous collector but retrofit call cancellation wiring matters.

emily: We use `mapLatest` then `flatMapConcat { flowOf(api.getData()) }` and `collectLatest { ... }`. Version: Retrofit 2.9 + OkHttp 4.11 + Kotlin coroutines 1.6.

theo: That composition can resubscribe on upstream error and if the token refresh logic races with retryOnConnectionFailure you can get duplicate refreshes. Are you using an interceptor to handle 401 and synchronously refresh token?

emily: Yes 	60s lock in TokenInterceptor: on 401 we call `refresh()` synchronously then retry the original request. It mostly works, but in the blip case two requests both get 401 and both attempt refresh concurrently. We tried synchronizing with an in-memory mutex but it didn't always prevent the second refresh on some devices.

alex: Device timing matters; if second request was queued in OkHttp prior to cancel it might still see 401. Two mitigations: 1) centralize token refresh with a single-producer queue (Channel/Mutex + suspend until resolved), 2) make interceptor check if a refresh is in-flight and await it instead of starting a new one.

emily: We implemented `refreshInProgress` AtomicReference and awaiters polling it; reduced dupes but still saw occasional second refresh when cancellation/resubscribe happened quickly.

raj: Polling is racy. Better pattern: have a `CompletableDeferred<Token>` that is set when refresh starts; others `await()` it. Example: `val refreshRef = AtomicReference<CompletableDeferred<Token>?>(null)` then first CAS creates CompletableDeferred and performs refresh completing it. Others get the ref and `await()`.

theo: Also consider disabling `retryOnConnectionFailure` on the client used for auth flows to avoid OkHttp silently replaying the request under the hood. If the original 401 was from a partial write or connection error, replay semantics can trigger multiple attempts.

emily: Good point. We had retryOnConnectionFailure=true globally. Switching it off for the auth client plus the CompletableDeferred fixed our repro on device lab (Pixel 6 / API 33).

alex: For onboarding docs: show a robust token refresh pattern (CompletableDeferred example) and recommend `retryOnConnectionFailure(false)` for auth clients and avoiding streaming in auth requests. Also add a small note about Flow re-subscription semantics and using stable upstream operators.

ci-bot: CI: reproduce job created https://ci.internal/repro/2478001234-1 with a device matrix and a tiny repro.

emily: I'll push the sample patch: 1) add the CompletableDeferred-based refresh helper, 2) create a dedicated auth OkHttpClient with retryOnConnectionFailure=false, 3) add a unit test that simulates a blip and asserts single refresh. Will add docs change for DX.

raj: Nice. Also include an integration test in device CI that cancels and re-collects quickly to catch regressions.

emily: Will do. Thanks all.
